problem:
Suppose that the following elementary row operations, in the given order, are to be applied to a $2\times 2$ matrix $A:$

$$
{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1},\,{R}_{2}:=\frac{1}{5}{R}_{2}
$$

Find the equivalent notation in terms of matrix multiplication.
worked_solution:
First, let's find the elementary matrices corresponding to the two given elementary row operations

- The first elementary row operation is ${R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1}.$ The  corresponding elementary matrix can be found by applying this same elementary row operation to the identity matrix as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & ={E}_{1}\end{aligned}
$$

- The second elementary row operation is ${R}_{2}:=\frac{1}{5}{R}_{2}$ The  corresponding elementary matrix can be found by applying this same elementary row operation to the identity matrix as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2}:=\frac{1}{5}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & \frac{1}{5}\end{aligned}] \\  & ={E}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

To apply the first elementary row operation to the matrix $A,$ we multiply by ${E}_{1}$ on the left and get ${E}_{1}A:$ 

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot A
$$

Then, to apply the second elementary row operation to ${E}_{1}A,$ we multiply by ${E}_{2}$ on the left and get ${E}_{2}{E}_{1}A:$ 

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & \frac{1}{5}\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot A
$$
